ops.new_text: The other three arms were scored at every level of the sweep, and Supplementary S9 reports all five (Table S9, computed from the registered per-seed files by `tools/make_table_s9.py`). Decoder width on its own does not reproduce the advantage: B_wide led B by between −0.12 and −0.01 points across the seven levels (−0.124 points at 20 dB, CI −0.510 to +0.240, 28 of 58 seeds), and C_wide led C by at most +0.03 points (+0.034 at 20 dB, CI −0.387 to +0.452, 28 of 58 seeds; the values at 35, 30 and 25 dB are in Table S9). The branch without the width control, D minus B, tracks the registered contrast level for level, reaching +1.973 points at 20 dB (CI +1.616 to +2.327, 54 of 58 seeds) against +2.097 for D minus B_wide, and the late split, C_wide minus B_wide, reached +0.425 points at 20 dB (CI +0.005 to +0.862). The evaluation-only advantage therefore belongs to the position of the split, not to decoder width; replacing B with the widened control B_wide adds between 0.01 and 0.12 points to it across the levels and removes none of it.

The primary endpoint is heart-channel Dice on the quarter-amplitude set (EIDORS `calc_hm_set(img, 0.25)`), computed on the test split and averaged over seeds. Differences between arms are reported in Dice points, hundredths of the Dice coefficient. Secondary outcomes are mean absolute error (MAE), intersection over union (IoU), sensitivity, specificity, average symmetric surface distance (ASSD) and the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), the same set on the lung channel, and the sweep. Seeds are the unit of replication, and every contrast is paired within seed. Because every seed is scored on the same 360 test geometries, the seed-level bootstrap intervals reported throughout describe training-run variability, not variability over test geometries. A geometry-level interval for the three main contrasts is reported beside the seed-level one in Section 3.5 and Supplementary S8. The registered rules are as follows. H1 (primary): D exceeds B_wide on heart Dice if the mean paired difference exceeds B_wide's seed-to-seed standard deviation and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (Wilcoxon, 1945) <!--ref:Wilcoxon1945--><!--anchor:none:--> over paired seeds gives p < 0.05. Otherwise H1 is falsified. The floor is there so that a difference smaller than the scatter between two training runs of the same architecture cannot be declared a success on a p-value alone. It states what size of effect would matter, and it was written before any effect was seen. The Wilcoxon test is two-sided and was computed with the asymptotic normal approximation without continuity correction, the default of the SciPy implementation above n = 50 and the procedure the scoring code applied. No paired difference was tied at zero, and W, the smaller signed-rank sum, is reported with p for every rule-bearing contrast. H2 (position): the same rule applied to D minus C_wide. H3 (noise): the paired difference D minus B_wide at the lowest SNR exceeds that at the highest, with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval on the difference-of-differences, resampling seeds, that excludes zero. H4 (lung): no difference is expected between arms, and the lung channel is reported, not tested. No multiplicity adjustment is applied: the four registered rules are separate pre-specified decisions, each with its own floor, H3 rests on one interval, and the per-level tests and intervals of the sweep are descriptive and reported with their unadjusted values. The onset in Section 3.2 is read from seven correlated levels; for reference, at the first level at which p falls below 0.05, 35 dB, p = 0.0011 is also below the Bonferroni threshold for seven tests, 0.05/7 = 0.0071. Effect sizes are reported as Cohen's dz for paired differences (Lakens, 2013) <!--ref:Lakens2013EffectSize--><!--anchor:none:-->, and the bootstrap intervals use 100,000 resamples of the 58 seeds, except those of Table S9 and of the width contrasts in Section 3.2 drawn from it, which use 20,000 (`tools/make_table_s9.py`).

The authors used Claude (Anthropic; Fable 5.1, Opus 5 and Opus 5.5, accessed August to October 2026) throughout this work. The assistant wrote the code in `tools/` that produced every reported number, figure and table, drafted and revised the manuscript text, ran the simulated peer-review panel recorded in the project repository, and carried out the citation verification reported in the same place. The authors defined the research questions, wrote and fixed the preregistrations before any result existed, made every design decision, and verified the results and the text.
